title: The link check sees an injection's point inside its target
text: A mixin's @At names a call or field use inside its target method (INVOKE, FIELD). JarPort checks that the named member exists in the new release, not that the new target method still uses it, so an injection whose point moved out of the method links and fails at start (Puzzle on 1.21.2: RenderSystem.blendFunc is no longer called in LoadingOverlay.render). GameDiff has every method's references in both releases, so the check can read the new body; a point that moved to a method the target calls is where a retarget would come from.
finish: exposure.py jars reports Puzzle's injection on 1.21.1 to 1.21.2 as unlinked, and exposure.py load finds no mod that links and fails in the client
wrongIf: the new check reports an injection point that Mixin finds
result: 2026-11-20: every injector (@Inject, @Redirect, @ModifyArg, @ModifyVariable, @WrapOperation and the other MixinExtras injectors) into a method that still links has its @At checked against the new method's own code: an INVOKE or FIELD point the old method used and the new one no longer uses (or not as often as its ordinal needs), and a @ModifyVariable LOAD or STORE ordinal beyond the new method's loads or stores of that type. Where the injector requires a place (its require, or its mixin config's injectors.defaultRequire) it is a break; otherwise a quiet hook, listed like an override the game no longer calls. Puzzle's LoadingOverlay hook on 1.21.2 is reported. Most mods that newly fail this check are real: 1.20.5 split Minecraft.disconnect, so Forge Config API Port's and FastQuit's required points are gone. Every update (tools/cloud-run exposure, run 44778079456): 5,854 -> 5,838 of 9,423 on main after #128; +1 from moved overrides (Fabric 1.19.4 -> 1.20) and -17 mods whose required injection point is gone (Better Mount HUD crashes on it in a real Fabric 1.20.5 client).
